Article Title: Punjab opens applications for second batch of anti-drug mental health fellowship
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Reinforcing its focus on tackling substance abuse through a rehabilitation-led approach, the Punjab government launched the Leadership in Mental Health Programme (LMHP), India's first fellowship against substance abuse, in February 2026. Thirteen fellows from the inaugural cohort are currently working across Punjab to strengthen mental healthcare services and support the state's anti-drug efforts.The fellows are deployed under the Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann-led Yudh Nashean Virudh campaign, helping integrate mental healthcare and community-based rehabilitation into the state's fight against drugs. The initiative aims to strengthen rehabilitation services while placing mental health at the centre of Punjab's anti-drug strategy.The government is now preparing to launch applications for the programme's second cohort, comprising 10 fellows and seven Senior Associates, with the goal of building a statewide network of trained young professionals across all 23 districts.Implemented by the Department of Health and Family Welfare in collaboration with the state's Data Intelligence and Technical Support Unit, the programme is designed to develop mental health leaders capable of driving evidence-based prevention, treatment and rehabilitation initiatives.The fellows, selected through a rigorous process, come from diverse fields including psychology, public health and social work and commit to supporting the state's anti-drug campaign for two years.As part of the programme, they receive intensive training in psychosocial interventions, relapse prevention, programme management, community-based rehabilitation and leadership. The training is delivered with support from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Mumbai, the programme's selection and knowledge partner.Health minister Balbir Singh said the fellowship seeks to combine leadership with empathy while strengthening Punjab's response to substance abuse. "Yudh Nashean Virudh is not just an initiative against drugs; it is a movement to reclaim Punjab's youth. While strict action is being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers, we are equally committed to helping every victim of drug abuse return to a life full of dignity and prevent the youth from falling into the trap of addiction. Leadership in Mental Health Programme reflects our belief that making Punjab addiction-free is possible only when enforcement, treatment, and prevention work hand-in-hand and backed by strong healthcare setup and community support," he said.The minister said addiction should be treated as a chronic health condition requiring sustained care. During their postings at district hospitals and de-addiction and rehabilitation centres, fellows work with patients and families, facilitate treatment, support relapse prevention and promote community-based rehabilitation. They also focus on reducing stigma, encouraging community participation and ensuring continuity of care after rehabilitation.Beyond district-level interventions, the first cohort is also supporting healthcare workers, strengthening service delivery and helping institutionalise best practices in Punjab's fight against substance abuse.According to the government, the programme is aimed at improving the way communities respond to substance use disorders by embedding mental health into the state's broader anti-drug campaign, with rehabilitation and long-term recovery forming a key part of the strategy.
Article Summary: The punjab government launched the leadership in mental health programme in february 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen rehabilitation services while placing mental health at the centre of punjab's anti-drug strategy. Thirteen fellows from the inaugural cohort are currently working across punjab to strengthen mental healthcare services.

Article Title: 'Head of family PM Modi listens': BJP's Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
Article Text:
BJP MP Raghav Chadha (ANI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. "Chadha stressed that the paper leak crisis could only be resolved through an "institutional solution" and not through "media sound-bytes", which he claimed was the approach adopted by the PM Modi-led government.BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome."Addressing NEET aspirants, he said, "Your anger is justified. Your pain is real. And your concerns about the examination system are genuine."He further said that when students raised their voices in protest, the Prime Minister listened and acted as a "guardian" to address their concerns."Students demanded, the government acted. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.
Article Summary: Bjp leader said, "i don't want headline, but an outcome" chadha led a rebel exodus from arvind kejriwal-founded aap, with seven rajya sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling bjp.

Article Title: 'First you broke their bones, now filing FIRs': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah to not 'threaten Gen Z into silence'
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi took a jab at PM Modi and Amit Shah, calling them 'India's past'

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the action against student protesters, alleging that the government was trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests.Making a statement on X, the Congress leader said, "PM Modi and Amit Shah - you cannot threaten Gen Z into silence. First you broke their bones. Now you are filing FIRs and taking down their accounts."Further taking a jab at PM Modi and Shah, he added, "You are India’s past. Be careful about how you treat India’s future."This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action against student protesters during the July 20 demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the Congress MP had called for an impartial probe into the alleged use of force, saying, "Students deserve justice. An independent SC-monitored high-powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students."Gandhi also shared a video purportedly showing police action against the protesters. The footage appeared to show police personnel lathi-charging demonstrators, while another clip showed a man in civilian clothes forcefully pushing a student carrying the Indian flag onto the road.His demand came as Opposition MPs from several INDIA bloc parties staged a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex over the alleged police action against students and the alleged embezzlement of donations meant for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.The MPs gathered around 10.30 am, carrying placards questioning who ordered the police action at Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding accountability from the Centre over the alleged use of force and the alleged financial irregularities in donations to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.The protest took place hours before the Rajya Sabha was scheduled to consider and pass the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi took a jab at pm modi and amit shah, calling them 'india's past' this comes a day after rahul demanded a supreme court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action. Article Title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge speaks in Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: The debate on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill in RS Thursday turned into a heated argument between treasury benches and opposition when leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti.Kharge alleged portions of Manusmriti have become part of the "curriculum" under BJP govt. He was challenged by leader of the House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.RS chairperson CP Radhakrishnan asked Kharge what Manusmriti had to do with the bill. Kharge claimed, "Manusmriti teaches that if a 'Shudra' listens to Veda, his ears should be filled with shards; if he reads Ved aloud, his tongue should be cut off; and if he retains its words, his body should be dismembered."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Kharge citing B R Ambedkar's writings to argue there was no untouchability in the era of Manu.
Article Summary: Opposition leader of the opposition mallikarjun kharge read out what he claimed hindi translation of a portion from manusmriti. He was challenged by leader of house j p nadda, who asked the lop to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.

Article Title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP

NEW DELHI: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests, as they highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns by holding dialogue with students to end their agitation and proposing a stronger law against exam paper leaks.Participating in the discussion, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest and also highlighted how senior ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh held talks with them and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was fasting for 26 days.Government agreed to the demands of students, he said, adding Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, a fast-track court was set up and a task force was set up by PM Narendra Modi under Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.On Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Trivedi said there are three basic principles - a sensitive approach towards students, a secured process and a stringent law against paper leaks. Article Title: Gujarat restores 94% flood-hit roads as IMD warns of fresh spell; Ahmedabad advises WFH
Article Text:
Gujarat is restoring infrastructure and providing aid after unprecedented torrential rains

Road connectivity restored across Gujarat

Relief package extended to Valsad, Navsari

Surat on red alert as fresh weather system approaches

Ahmedabad issues work-from-home advisory





AHMEDABAD: Gujarat has launched a massive restoration and relief exercise after an unprecedented spell of torrential rain battered large parts of the state.Authorities are now preparing for another round of extremely heavy rainfall expected over the next three days.The roads and buildings department said it had restored connectivity on nearly 94% of the roads damaged or closed due to flooding, while the state government announced financial assistance for flood-hit traders, transporters and farmers.Meanwhile, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) urged residents to work from home on Friday and Saturday after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for the city.Heavy rainfall between July 23 and 27 triggered widespread flooding, waterlogging and infrastructure damage across Gujarat, forcing the closure of 1,540 roads.According to the chief minister’s office, restoration teams worked round the clock to reopen 1,451 roads, restoring nearly 94 per cent of the affected network within days, news agency ANI reported.South Gujarat was the worst-hit region, accounting for 1,251 road closures.Of these, 1,236 roads have already been reopened, with traffic restored on 1,187 roads within 24 to 48 hours.The restoration drive was carried out under the guidance of chief minister Bhupendra Patel, with over 1,400 personnel, including 145 technical officers and 1,316 field staff, deployed across affected districts.The department also pressed into service more than 300 heavy machines, including 195 JCBs, 86 tractors and 59 dumpers, to clear debris and repair damaged stretches.A State Flood Control Cell monitored the situation every two hours, while six specialised engineering teams assessed the structural safety of government buildings and bridges in flood-hit districts, ANI reported.State minister Jitu Vaghani said traders, truck owners and others affected by the floods in Valsad and Navsari districts would receive financial assistance on the same lines as the relief package announced earlier for Surat and Ahmedabad.According to an official release, around 18,000 beneficiaries in Valsad have already received relief, including Rs 3.5 crore in cash assistance, Rs 9.5 crore towards household losses and housing aid, PTI reported.Vaghani said immediate surveys would be conducted to assess crop losses, after which compensation would be provided under state and central government norms.He added that district collectors had been authorised to take urgent decisions to address fodder shortages, while scientific measures would also be undertaken to save damaged orchards and plantations.Valsad and Navsari were among the worst-affected districts during the recent rains, with Umbergaon taluka recording over 1,100 mm of rainfall in just over 48 hours, triggering widespread flooding and affecting lakhs of residents.Surat has also been placed on high alert after a weather system originating over the Bay of Bengal began moving towards Gujarat.Surat Municipal commissioner M Nagarajan said a red alert had been issued for the city and district, following directions from the State Emergency Operations Centre, PTI reported.“NDRF and SDRF teams are already on standby, and additional teams can be deployed immediately if required. We are leaving no stone unturned to ensure a prompt response to any exigency,” Nagarajan said.As part of precautionary measures, the Surat Municipal Corporation has removed 150 hoardings and 100 hazardous trees, secured high-mast towers across the city and opened shelter homes in low-lying areas for residents who may need to be evacuated.The IMD said a deep depression over west-central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Vidarbha and southeast Madhya Pradesh is expected to move westwards towards Gujarat while gradually weakening.The weather office also said the monsoon trough remains active south of its normal position, with an east-west shear zone persisting across central India, creating favourable conditions for widespread rainfall.Authorities have forecast another spell of heavy to very heavy rainfall between July 31 and August 1, with isolated places likely to receive extremely to exceptionally heavy rainfall on Friday.Surat, Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Bhavnagar, Bharuch, Narmada, Tapi and Dangs are among the districts expected to witness intense showers over the next three days.With another spell of heavy rain forecast, the AMC issued an advisory urging residents to work from home on Friday and Saturday.Municipal commissioner Banchha Nidhi Pani said all leave for civic officials had been cancelled and emergency control rooms activated across the city.“We are appealing to citizens to work from home on both days,” he said, adding that people should avoid parking vehicles in flood-prone basements and stay away from trees and hoardings during strong winds.The civic body has converted municipal schools and community halls into emergency shelters and kept 245 stormwater pumping stations and 315 drainage pumping stations operational.Officials said the Sabarmati river had been drained by opening all gates of the Vasna Barrage to create additional storage capacity for incoming rainwater, while water supply to the Kharicut Canal had been suspended as a precaution.The AMC has also identified 147 waterlogging-prone locations and deployed teams to monitor them round the clock.Residents of low-lying areas will be shifted to safer places if flooding worsens.Mayor Hitesh Barot said the city’s drainage network, canals and water bodies had been cleaned ahead of the expected rainfall, with workers and pumping equipment positioned at vulnerable locations.
Article Summary: Gujarat is restoring infrastructure and providing aid after unprecedented torrential rains. Roads and buildings department said it had restored connectivity on nearly 94% of the roads damaged or closed due to flooding. The state government announced financial assistance for flood-hit traders, transporters and farmers.

Article Title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.
Article Summary: Bjp mp bansuri swaraj uses gen z-style praise for pm during anti-paper leak bill debate. Pm narendra modi announced formation of high-powered task force to overhaul india's examination system. The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the neet row.

Article Title: Rs 28.5 crore cash, Rs 21.5 crore gold: Police raid retired bus driver's house in West Bengal
Article Text:
Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.





SURI: Birbhum police on Wednesday raided the house of a retired govt bus driver in Deucha village and seized gold bars and biscuits worth around Rs 21.5 crore, along with two trunkloads of cash. The cash haul had crossed Rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted.Officers said Minar Mondal, owner of the two-storey house and a relative of influential stone trader Tulu Mondal, and his son were being questioned about the source of the seized wealth and whether they had stashed money and gold at any other location.Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.The entire area was cordoned off for the search, which began in the early hours. Several high-ranking district police officers, including ASP Nilesh Gaikwad and DSP (law and order) Kunal Mukherjee, supervised the raid.Minar’s kin Tulu Mondal, a prominent stone trader in the district, was a stone revenue collector during the tenure of the Trinamool govt. Sources said that after retiring from his govt job, Minar was assigned a key responsibility by Tulu.“Minar was in charge of collecting revenue from stone-filled trucks at one of the seven toll gates in the quarry belt of Deucha. Investigators are trying to find out whether he had siphoned off a chunk of the money meant for the govt coffers,” a source said.Tulu was considered a close associate of Anubrata Mondal, once a Trinamool strongman in the district. He was accused of operating illegal stone quarries and implicated in a cattle smuggling case.ED had raided his home and office in 2022. Within 48 hours of the raid, the district police arrested him in a murder case. He was released on bail and allegedly went into hiding after the assembly poll results were declared on May 4.Tulu had grabbed eyeballs in Dec 2024 by hosting a lavish reception for his daughter’s wedding. Celebrities from Bollywood and the Bengali entertainment industry attended the reception in an extravagant venue modelled on the iconic Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur.CM Suvendu Adhikari thanked police for Wednesday’s operation.He posted on X, “The work of our law enforcement agencies in taking strict action against the sand mafia is commendable. Birbhum Police conducted a major raid at the hideout of illegal operator Tulu Mondal — alias Mohammad Najibuddin — in the Mohammad Bazar police station area.”He wrote, “Let it be unequivocally clear: no person with a chequered past who has amassed wealth through the exploitation of public resources and hobnobbing with the then ruling political party will be spared.”He commended the director general of police, superintendent of Birbhum police and district police personnel for the success of the operation.Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson for the Trinamool faction loyal to Mamata Banerjee, said that while those responsible for such crimes should not be spared, the govt should also investigate netas who allegedly patronised such activities.“I hear that those responsible for such crimes were closely linked to netas who now brand themselves as ‘good Trinamool’. I will urge the govt to delve deeper and identify those who shielded such criminals and benefited from their illegal earnings,” he said.
Article Summary: Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul. The cash haul had crossed rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted. Officers said minar mondal, owner of the two-storey house, and his son were being questioned about the source of the seized wealth.

Article Title: ‘Normal’ July rain defies forecast of El Nino impact
Article Text:
Monsoon in India (representative image)

El Niño alone can no more explain India’s rain pattern: Experts

India’s monsoon has delivered a surprise this July, defying forecasts of below-normal rainfall despite a strengthening El Nino and reinforcing scientists’ warnings that climate change is altering the country’s most important weather system, report Chittaranjan Tembhekar & Gaurav Talwar.As of July 30, India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. IMD had said July rainfall was likely to be less than 94% of long period average.However, rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.The monsoon deficit since June 1 was 14%. The unexpected turnaround in July has eased fears of a big monsoon shortfall but highlighted a new reality: long dry spells interspersed with short bursts of extremely heavy rain capable of triggering floods and landslides.According to a Climate Trends briefing, successive weather systems cut the national rainfall deficit considerably from 40% at the end of June.Scientists say the biggest lesson from monsoon 2026 is that El Niño alone can no longer explain India’s rainfall behaviour.Global warming, warming oceans and changing atmospheric circulation are increasingly interacting with traditional climate drivers, making monsoon forecasts more difficult.“The challenge is no longer predicting how much rain India will receive, but forecasting where, when and how intensely it will fall in a warming climate,” scientists said.Rainfall remained highly uneven. While 16 meteorological subdivisions states recorded normal rainfall in the season and three saw excess to large-excess rainfall, 17 subdivisions remained deficient. Central India was almost normal with a 1% surplus, northwest India had an 11% shortfall, while east and northeast India remained 30% below normal and south India 25% deficient.The findings are particularly striking because the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has projected an 81% probability of a very strong El Niño developing between Oct and Dec — a pattern usually associated with weaker Indian monsoons.Former IMD director general K J Ramesh attributed July’s recovery to abnormal warming over the western Pacific, which spawned successive monsoon systems over the Bay of Bengal, and the increasing influence of Western Disturbances that enhanced rainfall over Maharashtra and Gujarat.“Climate change is reshaping the characteristics of the monsoon, which existing models are failing to take into account,” Ramesh said.Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading said the monsoon rebounded rapidly after an early July lull. He cited Umbergaon in Gujarat receiving 1,064 mm of rain in 24 hours —among the highest daily totals recorded since 1901 — as evidence of intensifying rainfall extremes, adding that climate change appears to be amplifying the monsoon’s internal weather systems.
Article Summary: India received 270.1mm of rains in july against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. But rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central india receiving 29% excess in july while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.

Article Title: Anti-paper leak bill clears Parliament; PM Modi says it will build a credible exam system
Article Text:
Amid opposition’s walkout, Rajya Sabha clears it by voice vote

NEW DELHI: Parliament on Thursday approved a bill to amend the anti-paper leak law, prescribing stricter punishment, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi saying an important step towards building a credible exam system has been taken.In a selfie-video message, the Prime Minister asserted that gangs behind exam paper leaks, which play with the future of students, will not be spared, and stringent laws are needed to deal with them. "Our work will continue and we will not allow this situation to persist for long," he said.For the past many decades every state govt and the Centre have faced this menace of paper leaks, which is posing a crisis for students, the PM said about the bill that proposes a longer jail term and steeper fine. "It has become necessary to bring reforms in the education system in all states and at the Centre," Modi said, asking the youth to work together with govt to fulfil the dream of a developed India.His government, he said, has taken a series of steps for reforming the exam system, be it forming a task force, constituting fast-track courts or taking into consideration the views of states. Optimal use of technology is necessary, he added.Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, was cleared by voice vote in RS amid a walkout by a large section of the opposition, a day after it was passed by LS. This will become a law after the President's assent.Replying to the discussion on the bill in Rajya Sabha, Union minister Jitendra Singh highlighted measures taken by govt in the education sector, including NEP-2020 and an increase in the number of universities.Earlier in the day, Singh had told the Upper House that the bill testifies the govt does not stand on prestige and is open to healthy inputs. "We are open to constructive suggestions from all quarters, and that's exactly the reason why, in the wake of the recent sequence of events, the PM lost no time to declare that nobody will be allowed to jeopardise the future of our children and also announced the resolve of zero tolerance to paper leaks," he said.According to the bill, individuals involved in paper leaks or unfair means in exams will get jail terms for a minimum of five years and a maximum of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh. For organised crimes, it proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. The bill also seeks to empower all state govts and UT administrations to designate any court of session as a special fast-track court to try offences under the proposed law.The bill also empowers the central govt to constitute a special task force for the investigation of any offence, if necessary.
Article Summary: Rajya sabha clears it by voice vote, amid opposition’s walkout. Pm narendra modi: "our work will continue and we will not allow this situation to persist for long" bill proposes a longer jail term and steeper fine.

Article Title: 2 years after death, Supreme Court clears former PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
Article Text:
File photo: Former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A delhi court sensationally summoned former pm manmohan singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. A bench of justices v gopala gowda and c nagappan had on april 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

Article Title: 215 academicians slam Priyanka for 'gaumutra' remark

NEW DELHI: Over 200 academicians have written an open letter objecting to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra 's 'gaumutra' expert jibe at IIT Madras director V Kamakoti and said dismissing a scholar through a label risks undermining the scientific temper promoted by the Constitution.The first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, is credited with popularising the term 'scientific temper', and the 215 academicians have invoked it to criticise Priyanka, saying scientists, scholars and educators deserve to know that they can participate in public debate without fear of being reduced to dismissive labels.They defended Kamakoti's advocacy of cow urine, which is traditionally associated with some therapeutic benefits, and said scientific temper is not merely scepticism towards unconventional ideas but also the willingness to examine claims objectively before accepting or rejecting them. "History reminds us that many ideas once considered implausible eventually found scientific validation, while many widely accepted beliefs were later discarded," they said."When complex scientific questions become objects of political ridicule, society loses an opportunity for informed debate. In a democracy, disagreement is essential. Mockery is not a substitute for reasoned engagement," they added.Kamakoti, they noted, has been a guiding force behind India's first industry-grade microprocessor, and he is one of the top tech brains in the country.Addressing the Congress MP, the academicians said, "Whether intended as sarcasm or political rhetoric, such a characterisation raises concerns that go far beyond one individual."Kamakoti is a member of the six-member task force on exam reforms constituted by the Centre after the NEET paper leak row and was at the receiving end of Priyanka's dig during a debate in Lok Sabha over a bill making punishment in paper leak cases more stringent.
Article Summary: Over 200 academicians have written an open letter objecting to priyanka gandhi vadra's 'gaumutra' jibe at iit madras director v kamakoti. The first prime minister, jawaharlal nehru, is credited with popularising the term'scientific temper'

Article Title: Despite unrest, PM Modi, Amit Shah haven't spoken on NEET protests: Opposition

Article Title: Supreme Court: No blanket ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control
Article Text:
File photo: Pellet gun use during jantar mantar protest

Both protesters and police human beings: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed Delhi government to provide treatment to those injured during students’ protests but found a plea for ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control vague and asked when police are permitted to fire bullets in extreme situations, how could pellet guns be banned.Appearing for petitioners, advocate Vrinda Grover questioned the legality of Rapid Action Force using pellet guns against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar, and urged the SC to direct the Union govt to preserve the ammunition log of RAF during their deployment at the protest site and award exemplary compensation to those injured by metallic pellets.The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20, and former IPS officer Yashovardhan Azad.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed preservation of the logbook, and solicitor general Tushar Mehta said all documents required for an effective investigation into alleged police excesses and violence at the protest site would be preserved.When Grover persisted with the plea for a ban on use of pellet guns, Justice Bagchi termed the prayer vague and said, “Police regulations permit use of pellet guns in exceptional circumstances.If you want phasing out of pellet guns, then you must challenge those regulations, which you have not done.“You say at no stage metallic pellet can be used, when graded response permits use of bullets in extreme situations. Seeking ban on use of pellet guns cannot be on the same plane as seeking a ban on use of bullets (for crowd dispersal)? Law permits use of bullets.”Justice Bagchi recalled a Calcutta High Court order quashing a colonial-era police regulation asking personnel to fire at chests instead of legs of protesters to save ammunition.The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for police’s graded action delineating when to use rubber pellets followed by metallic pellets. Grover agreed to amend the prayer to enable the SC to provide guidelines for the police’s crowd dispersal action.The bench reiterated that there were occasions when peaceful protests were hijacked by miscreants and became vehicles for ulterior purposes, including for the purpose of sabotaging the bona fide aim of the protests.“All such situations would require various graded responses. But most important is to equip police with adequate safety gear. Only then can they ponder over graded responses to violent crowds. Otherwise, the protesters and police, both are human beings and react equally to threats coming to them,” the bench said. The SG said citizens always have a right to non-violent protest.Grover said updated guidelines framed by Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPRD) were not available after 2016 and it was very difficult to obtain information from police. The bench said this was not correct and such guidelines should be uploaded on websites. The SG said he would check the veracity of Azad’s allegation.The SC had said on July 28 that it was prima facie convinced about a high-level inquiry into alleged police excesses and violence against cops and directed police to preserve data collected from various cameras but restrained them from taking coercive action against students and making public their personal data.Grover said petitioners Mansoori and Singh were injured by metallic pellets fired by RAF without provocation. She said while Mansoori received good treatment at Lady Hardinge Hospital, Singh did not, leading the SC to direct Delhi govt to provide adequate treatment to the two and all those injured during the protests led by CJP.
Article Summary: The petition was filed by sheikh irshad mansoori and prashant kumar singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on july 20. A bench of chief justice surya kant and justices joymalya bagchi and v mohana directed preservation of the logbook.

Article Title: Release 3,500 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu: Cauvery authority to Karnataka
Article Text:
Cauvery Water Management Authority upholds Karnataka water release directive to Tamil Nadu

NEW DELHI: Upholding the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee's order, Cauvery Water Management Authority on Thursday directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu for the next 15 days. As per the direction, Karnataka will have to release a total of 4 TMC (thousand million cubic) feet of river water to the neighbouring state.The decision came after an emergency meeting convened by the authority to consider Karnataka's appeal against the committee's Wednesday order. The meeting was called as Karnataka appealed to the authority against the order, taking the plea that 'below normal' monsoon rainfall had depleted reservoir levels and that drought conditions prevailed in the state.State officials are learnt to have told the authority that Cauvery basin reservoirs in Karnataka currently held around 36.7 TMC of water, which was substantially lower than the 99 TMC recorded during corresponding period last year. They pleaded that it would be difficult to even meet drinking water requirements and other essential needs in the present situation.Tamil Nadu's representatives, however, opposed Karnataka's plea, arguing that the committee's recommendation dealt with only the minimum quantity that should be released. They pointed out that the reservoirs had enough flow and alleged that Karnataka had failed to properly implement the distress-sharing formula prescribed in the situation of deficient rainfall in a particular year.
Article Summary: Cauvery water management authority upholds karnataka water release directive to tamil nadu. As per the direction, karnataka will have to release a total of 4 tmc (thousand million cubic) feet of river water to the neighbouring state. The meeting was called as karnataka appealed to the authority against the order.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi under fire: Anurag Thakur moves privilege notice over Lok Sabha speech
Article Text:
Rahul faces privilege notice: Anurag Thakur seeks action over 'unparliamentary' remarks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union minister Anurag Thakur on Thursday moved a privilege motion against Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , accusing him of using unparliamentary and derogatory expressions during the Monsoon Session and violating the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the house.In a notice submitted under Rules 222 and 223 of the Lok Sabha Rules, Thakur requested that the matter be admitted and referred to the Committee of Privileges for a detailed examination under Rule 227."Shri Rahul Gandhi has committed Breach of Privilege of member of Lok Sabha, Contempt of Lok Sabha and utter disregard to the authority of Hon'ble Speaker," the notice alleged.The move comes after Rahul Gandhi alleged that he was not allowed to speak during the debate on the anti-paper leak Bill and later repeated the claim at a press conference outside Parliament.In the privilege notice, Thakur alleged that Rahul Gandhi used expressions that were objected to by parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju during his speech in the Lok Sabha and continued using them despite objections and warnings from the Chair."Terming a section of citizens through such expressions on the floor of the House is offensive, derogatory, and demeans the dignity of Parliament, constituting contempt of the House," the notice stated.According to the notice, the remarks violated Rule 352 of the Rules of Procedure, which prohibits offensive and defamatory expressions, personal references questioning the bona fides of individuals, and remarks that demean any individual or class of persons.Thakur further alleged that Rahul Gandhi's conduct disrupted the functioning of the House and disregarded repeated directions from the Chair."He has conducted and behaved in the House in such a manner that it was obstructive in proper discharge of function of members of Lok Sabha individually and collectively as a House. He also did not follow the repeated instructions of the Hon'ble Speaker of the House," the notice said.The BJP leader alleged that Rahul Gandhi had committed a breach of privilege and contempt of the House and sought expunction of the disputed remarks from the official proceedings under Rules 380 and 381.The notice also requested that the matter be referred to the Committee of Privileges for a detailed inquiry and that Rahul Gandhi be directed to tender an unconditional apology to the House and the Union home minister.The development comes amid continuing political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the Opposition over the alleged NEET paper leak, police action against student protesters and repeated disruptions during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.
Article Summary: Rahul faces privilege notice: anurag thakur seeks action over 'unparliamentary' remarks. Rahul gandhi alleged that he was not allowed to speak during the debate on the anti-paper leak bill and later repeated the claim at a press conference outside parliament.
